title: CleanGutters Lighting vs JD Power Washing: Gutter Services Compared
body_markdown:
Choose **CleanGutters Lighting** if you want gutter cleaning, repairs, and stainless steel micro-mesh guard installation from a provider serving your region; choose **JD Power Washing** if its written proposal is the better match for a cleaning-only job. This comparison separates confirmed services from the details you need in writing before hiring either company.


**TL;DR**

- CleanGutters Lighting fits homeowners seeking gutter cleaning, repairs, and micro-mesh gutter protection.
- For cleangutters lighting vs jd power washing, compare written gutter-service scopes rather than company names.
- JD Power Washing belongs on your shortlist when its proposal matches your cleaning-only requirements.
- Compare installation details, warranty exclusions, and maintenance responsibilities before choosing gutter guards.


## Why this matters

A gutter cleaning and a gutter-protection installation solve different problems. Cleaning removes accumulated debris; guards address debris entry. Neither replaces correcting a loose gutter, a leaking connection, or a drainage problem.

For your 2026 comparison, start with the job your house needs—not the longest service list. The [gutter services overview](https://cleangutterslighting.com/services) is a starting point for checking the local specialist’s scope, but your written proposal should identify the work included at your property.

**The right contractor is the one whose written scope matches the gutter problem you need fixed.** A cleaning-only homeowner should not compare a debris-removal quote directly with a guard-installation proposal and treat them as equivalent jobs.

## At a glance

The confirmed service and warranty details below describe the local specialist. The JD Power Washing column identifies what its proposal needs to establish; it does not assign unverified services, materials, or policies to that company.

| Dimension | CleanGutters Lighting | JD Power Washing |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Homeowners seeking cleaning, repairs, and micro-mesh gutter protection | Cleaning-only shoppers when its written proposal meets their requirements |
| Service scope | Gutter cleaning, repair, and guard installation | Confirm the exact gutter work included |
| Standout feature | Surgical stainless steel micro-mesh gutter protection | Compare the proposed cleaning method and completion checks |
| Installation responsibility | Brand states Alex personally installs every job, without subcontractors | Confirm who performs the proposed work |
| Service area | South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware | Confirm coverage for your address |
| Warranty | Transferable lifetime warranties associated with gutter protection | Request any applicable written warranty terms |
| Maintenance expectations | Confirm inspection and upkeep requirements for the installed guards | Confirm what happens after cleaning and how repeat service is arranged |
| Pricing model | Request separate scopes for cleaning, repair, and installation | Request the charging basis for the proposed gutter work |

## The local specialist is the clearer fit for a guard project

**CleanGutters Lighting is the better-documented fit for homeowners seeking micro-mesh gutter protection.** Its stated offering includes guard installation alongside professional gutter cleaning and repair. That gives you a confirmed starting point when your goal is protection rather than another debris-removal visit.

The limitation is equally important: a broader service offering does not make a guard installation necessary. If your immediate problem is accumulated leaves, ask the contractor to distinguish the cleaning required now from any optional protection work.

For JD Power Washing, make the decision conditional on the actual proposal. If you want only a cleaning and its scope covers that job clearly, you have a relevant alternative. Do not infer guard-installation expertise—or its absence—from the company name.

Ask each contractor to separate these **3 gutter services**:

- **Cleaning:** What debris removal and drainage checks are included?
- **Repair:** Which defects will be corrected, and which remain outside the job?
- **Guard installation:** What material, attachment method, and upkeep requirements apply?

This separation keeps an optional upgrade from obscuring the work your gutters already need.

## Micro-mesh is a confirmed specification, not a universal winner

The local specialist identifies surgical stainless steel micro-mesh as its gutter-protection material. That is a concrete specification you can compare against another written proposal. It is not proof that every installation will suit every roof or debris condition.

Micro-mesh guards place a fine barrier over the gutter opening to help separate debris from entering water. The installation still needs to suit the existing gutter and roof edge. Surface debris and drainage conditions remain part of the maintenance discussion.

When reviewing JD Power Washing’s proposal, first establish whether protection is included at all. If the proposal covers cleaning only, a material comparison is irrelevant; compare the cleaning scopes instead.

For any guard proposal, ask:

- What is the mesh material?
- How is the guard attached?
- What happens at corners, ends, and roof valleys?
- What work is needed before installation?
- What maintenance remains your responsibility?

**A named material is useful; a complete installation specification is more useful.** Do not accept a material description as a substitute for explaining how the system will fit your house.

## The owner-installed commitment makes accountability clearer

The local specialist states that Alex installs every job personally rather than using subcontractors. For a homeowner buying an installation, that identifies who is responsible for carrying out the work. Ask for the same clarity in the proposal and scheduling conversation.

That commitment does not eliminate the need for documentation. Your scope should still identify the installation work, existing defects, cleanup responsibilities, and the process for reporting a problem afterward.

JD Power Washing earns consideration on this dimension when its proposal clearly identifies who performs the work and who handles callbacks. Without those details, assigning an installation-quality winner would be guesswork.

Separate **2 responsibilities** before you sign:

- **Work performed:** Who cleans, repairs, or installs at the house?
- **Follow-up handled:** Who responds if the agreed work needs attention?

An identifiable installer is a practical advantage. A clear follow-up process turns that advantage into something you can use after the crew leaves.

## Regional coverage favors the confirmed local option

South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware are the local specialist’s stated service regions. If your home is in those areas, the offering is geographically relevant. Confirm your exact address before discussing installation dates.

JD Power Washing should be assessed against the same address-level requirement. A familiar business name or nearby search result is not confirmation that a contractor serves your property or accepts the particular job you need.

For your 2026 shortlist, verify:

- Whether the contractor serves your address.
- Whether the visit covers cleaning, repairs, installation, or a combination.
- Whether any access limitations change the proposed scope.
- Who coordinates follow-up work at that address.

**Coverage is a screening question, not a craftsmanship score.** Once both contractors confirm the location, move on to the actual work and accountability rather than treating geography as proof of quality.

## The stated lifetime warranty needs a written comparison

Transferable lifetime warranties are part of the local specialist’s stated gutter-protection offering. That matters when you are evaluating a lasting installation, particularly if transfer rights form part of your decision.

The phrase alone does not establish every covered event. Ask for the warranty document and distinguish material coverage, installation coverage, exclusions, maintenance obligations, and transfer conditions. Do not assume that a protection warranty covers every drainage problem at the house.

For JD Power Washing, request the terms that apply to the proposed work. A cleaning job and a guard installation have different scopes; comparing their warranty labels without reading what each covers tells you little.

In 2026, make the warranty comparison about enforceable details:

- What specific problem triggers coverage?
- Who provides the remedy?
- What must the homeowner maintain or document?
- What steps apply when ownership changes?

**The local specialist has a stated transferable warranty offering; the written terms determine its practical value.** Keep a copy with the final scope rather than relying on a sales explanation.

## Neither contractor gets a maintenance-free pass

Guard installation and gutter cleaning do not remove the need to pay attention to drainage. A guard changes how debris reaches the gutter; cleaning removes debris already present. Neither description establishes that future inspection is unnecessary.

For a cleaning-only proposal, ask how completion is checked and whether downspout flow is addressed. For a guard proposal, ask what surface debris needs attention and what inspection the warranty requires.

These are different maintenance questions, not evidence that either company performs better. **Treat this dimension as a tie until the proposals explain your responsibilities.**

Before hiring, walk through the maintenance discussion in this order:

1. Identify the current blockage or overflow concern.
2. Confirm which work addresses that concern.
3. Record what remains outside the scope.
4. Ask what you should inspect afterward.
5. Keep the maintenance instructions with the warranty.


![Leaves resting above a generic mesh gutter cover beside a residential roof edge](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/b8b75feb-c558-4cce-bbe8-591c75f4e199/body-c9f02ee2ca529970c964c49689f55172.jpg)

*A gutter guard changes debris entry, but maintenance responsibilities still need to be explained.*


## Pricing: compare the job structure before the total

Neither company should receive a pricing-model advantage without a written proposal explaining how the work is charged. Ask whether the proposed amount covers a defined job, measured work, labor time, or separately approved repairs. Do not assume either business uses a particular model.

A defined cleaning scope makes the included work easier to compare. Separately authorized repair work gives you a decision point when a defect is identified. A combined cleaning-and-installation proposal needs clear boundaries so you can distinguish essential preparation from the guard installation itself.

For a useful 2026 comparison, request **1 written scope per contractor** describing:

- The gutters and downspouts included.
- Cleaning and disposal responsibilities.
- Named repairs and their authorization process.
- Guard materials and installation work, if applicable.
- Exclusions, completion checks, and follow-up terms.

**Predictability comes from a defined scope; flexibility comes from a clear change-approval process.** Neither is a reason to accept vague wording. Compare the same work before deciding which proposal offers better value.

## Final verdict: choose by the job, not the business name

### Choose CleanGutters Lighting for a protection-led project

**Best for: the homeowner seeking cleaning, repairs, and micro-mesh gutter protection in the stated service region.** The confirmed combination of services, stainless steel micro-mesh focus, owner-installed commitment, and transferable lifetime warranty offering makes this the clearer documented match for that project.

The tradeoff is that a protection-led proposal requires more decisions than a cleaning-only visit. Verify material details, preparation, exclusions, and maintenance before authorizing installation.

### Choose JD Power Washing when its cleaning scope wins

**Best for: the cleaning-only homeowner whose JD Power Washing proposal meets the required scope more clearly.** Choose that proposal when it identifies the included gutter work, completion checks, responsible crew, and follow-up terms better than the competing cleaning proposal.

That is a conditional recommendation, not a claim about services or results that have not been established. Do not buy a guard project simply because the other contractor offers one; buy the work your home needs.

| Dimension | Winner |
|---|---|
| Protection-led service fit | Local specialist, based on its confirmed offering |
| Documented guard material | Local specialist; compare any competing specification |
| Named installation responsibility | Local specialist’s stated owner-installed commitment |
| Confirmed regional coverage | Local specialist within its stated regions |
| Stated protection warranty | Local specialist; written terms still control |
| Maintenance expectations | Tie until responsibilities are documented |
| Pricing structure | Tie until equivalent scopes are supplied |
| Cleaning-only fit | JD Power Washing when its written scope is the better match |

## FAQ


**Is CleanGutters Lighting better than JD Power Washing for gutter guards?**

CleanGutters Lighting is the better-documented match for gutter guards because its stated services include surgical stainless steel micro-mesh installation. Compare any JD Power Washing guard proposal against the actual material, installation scope, and warranty rather than assuming equivalence.

**Which company should I choose if I only need gutter cleaning?**

Choose the contractor whose written cleaning scope best matches your house. Confirm debris removal, downspout checks, disposal, exclusions, and follow-up before deciding.

**Does JD Power Washing install micro-mesh gutter guards?**

Confirm guard installation directly with JD Power Washing before treating it as an available service. Request the material specification and installation terms in writing if protection is offered.

**Do micro-mesh gutter guards eliminate maintenance?**

Do not treat micro-mesh gutter guards as a promise of no maintenance. Ask what surface debris needs attention, what inspections are required, and how those responsibilities affect warranty coverage.

**What should a gutter-service proposal include in 2026?**

A 2026 gutter-service proposal should identify the work, materials, exclusions, responsible installer, and completion checks. Repairs and changes should have a clear approval process.

**What does a transferable lifetime gutter warranty cover?**

The written warranty defines coverage and transfer rights. Check covered defects, exclusions, homeowner responsibilities, remedy procedures, and any conditions that apply when the property changes owners.


## One last thing

Before approving your 2026 gutter project, ask the contractor to name the problem the proposed work will **not** fix. That answer separates a defined service from an open-ended promise—and gives you a clear boundary for judging the finished job.
